integrated tree, and you do not write files, create commits, run any git

driver's own suite result. When a plan document path is given, read it first.
The per-task referees each saw one diff against one task; you see the whole
tree against the whole plan, so your mandate is the two questions only the
integrated view can answer:

1. Claim: does the integrated tree do what each Claim says — the operator's
   own sentence, not only its Machine restatement? A deliverable that passes
   its own tests but does not meet its Claim is a finding.
2. Context: where two tasks carry the same literal (a schema, a file format, a
   constant), confirm both implementations agree with it and with each other.

The other slots are settled before you read, and re-deriving them here only
manufactures findings. The compiler derives the dependency edges, and the
integrated evidence below is what exercises the pairs they name. Each Proof
exam is written by the wave-0 examiner and run by the proof gate. A task that
did not land at all is recorded as a missing deliverable, so a tree without it
is already accounted for.

The INTEGRATED RUN EVIDENCE block, when present, is authoritative for every
`Run:` command it lists: the driver executed each one itself, on the adopted
integration tree. A request for their re-execution is settled by that block —
report what it shows; it is not a `deferredVerification` item, and `manual` is
for human judgment (aesthetic, product-fit), not for a command the driver ran.

content.text: Plan read. Now let me inspect the integrated tree.

I've read the plan, the three task contracts, and the integrated tree. Here's what I checked and found.

**Claim 1 — the PR body carries the residuals as a checklist.** `residual_items` (`fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:1170-1227`) reads `$EVIDENCE_DIR/$EVIDENCE_PATH/gate-receipt.json` and `report.json` through one `python3` reader, emitting `- [ ] deferred:external — …` for each `.gateCheck.acks[]` entry typed exactly `deferred:external`, `- [ ] critic — …` for each `minor` `completenessFindings` entry, and `- [ ] task <id> reviewer — <piece>` for each `; `-split note of each `done` task; newlines flatten to spaces. `render_card` (`:1390-1392`) emits the section only when non-empty, after the `### Plan` link line and before `plan_closes`, which stays last. To keep the excluded names out of the body at all, `receipt_fence` (`:1241-1263`) drops `gateCheck.acks` from the `### Checks` fence — the minimal change M1's "no line contains `runtime-only-B`" forces, and the receipt is still linked whole under `### Evidence`.

**Claim 2 — one follow-up issue listing the same items.** `file_followup` (`:1630-1669`) is called from `publish` after the `publish:pr` event and before the merge, so `do_boot`'s re-entry branch skips it; it returns early when `residual_items` prints nothing. Title `fleet $RUN_ID residuals: $(plan_title)`, labels `watch-item` plus `followup_labels`' kept names, body = `$PR_URL` + blank line + the same lines byte-for-byte (one shared function, not a restatement). A non-2xx or missing `html_url` is one `followup:` log line and `return 0`; a 2xx appends `publish:followup` with `url`/`items` and no `status.json` cell.

**Claim 3 — the contract names the sink.** `fleet/CONTRACT.md:271-287` carries the `### Residuals` sentence before the `Closes #<n>` lines, the `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues` filing with `watch-item` plus the six program labels, "never a gate", and `publish:followup` (`url`, `items`) with the count now reading `four event kinds`.
